Freixe de fulla estreta del Jardi Botanic Historic
trees.note: Count, not quality. This and the Acer below are the two remaining trees of the four the Catalan government declared monumental in April 2025, all four in the Sot de l'Estany ravine. We already publish the other two (bcn_005, bcn_006) and the city intro already tells the reader there are four. Adding both would put four of sixteen Barcelona entries inside one ravine behind one paid gate. Strong can

trees.name: Fals platan del Jardi Botanic Historic
trees.note: Same as above: the fourth monumental tree of the Sot de l'Estany, held back on count rather than merit. Register gives no planting year ('Per determinar'), so it would ship flagged.

trees.name: Camforer del Jardi Botanic Historic
trees.note: 1933, so 93 years, and a third entry inside the same paid garden. Ownership reads 'Privat' but that is the museum owning the land, not a closed gate, the same as bcn_006. Held on count and age, not access.

trees.name: Robinia del parc de la Ciutadella
trees.note: A 4.3 m trunk perimeter, which is large for a black locust, but the register's age field reads '100 anys' rather than a year, so there is no date to verify and no second source was found. Catalogued only in 2024, so press coverage may follow.

trees.name: Platan del parc de la Ciutadella
trees.note: 3.6 m girth and a 24 m crown, the biggest plane in the park, but the register carries no planting year at all and no second source dates it.

trees.name: Pitospor de la Ciutadella
trees.note: No planting year, no recorded height, and a 1.55 m girth on a species that is usually a shrub. Interesting as a curiosity, thin as a page.

trees.name: Araucaria de la casa de la Misericordia
trees.note: 27 m tall in the same courtyard as bcn_010, but the register gives no planting year and no independent source was found. It would also be a second entry on one small Raval courtyard.

trees.name: Platan oriental de la Universitat
trees.note: 1933, so 93 years, on a square rather than in a garden. A true Platanus orientalis rather than the usual London plane hybrid is genuinely uncommon in Spanish cities and this is worth a second look when Barcelona next grows. Would extend the Raval walk east to Placa de la Universitat.

trees.name: Alvocater de la placa de Can Bruixa
trees.note: An avocado tree 17 m tall in a Les Corts square is a good story, but 1945 makes it 81 years, under the bar, and its 0.8 m girth is slight. 465 m from bcn_007, so it would join that walk if the age bar ever softens.

trees.name: Huingan del carrer Joaquim Blume
trees.note: 1916, public, but a street tree with no second source found and little to say beyond the species.

trees.name: Taronger de Louisiana del carrer Maria Montessori
trees.note: 1948, 78 years. The same species as bcn_013 and younger; Barcelona does not need two Osage oranges.

trees.name: Castanyer bord de la placa Carles Buigas
trees.note: 1937, 89 years, under the bar.

trees.name: Ginjoler dels jardins Joan Maragall
trees.note: 1958, 68 years, well under the bar, and the Joan Maragall gardens open only at weekends.

trees.name: Ginkgo dels jardins de Mossen Cinto Verdaguer
trees.note: 1958, 68 years. Would carry an excellent autumn best_time if the age bar ever softened for a species this distinctive.

trees.name: Molle del jardi d'Aclimatacio and Eucaliptus tuart del jardi d'Aclimatacio
trees.note: Both dated 'Per determinar' in the register, both a short walk from bcn_005 and bcn_006. Two undated trees is not a walk.

trees.name: Garrofer del carrer Maignon
trees.note: Date is no longer the only open question: existence and species now have two sources (register 99400680090 plus beteve.cat's 2021 press coverage of the 40-tree AIL designation), but access is unconfirmed and leans against. The ajuntament's own description says the carob grows out of a roughly 2m wall 'that limits the internal road where cars circulate and the part of the garden at a higher level',

trees.name: Pebrer bord del carrer Maignon
trees.note: Same garden as the Garrofer above, 41m away, same access question and same conclusion: register plus beteve.cat's 2021 press piece give two sources for existence and species, but not for public access. Girth of 4.34m is large for the species; plausible for a mature multi-stemmed Schinus molle but worth a sanity check against a photo before shipping. Resolve alongside the Garrofer, they are one sit

trees.name: Arbres de l'amor de la placa Joanic
trees.note: 1956, 70 years. A Judas tree's April flowering would make a strong best_time, and it is 330 m from bcn_001, but it is too young.

trees.name: The Pedralbes cluster: Jardins del Palau Reial de Pedralbes and Jardins de la Torre Girona
trees.species: Pinus pinea; Cedrus deodara; Tetraclinis articulata; Brachychiton populneus; Maclura pomifera; Pinus halepensis
trees.note: Not evaluated in this pass, and recorded here because it is the strongest untouched cluster in the city. Eight register entries lie inside 400 m of each other across the Palau Reial gardens, the Torre Girona gardens and the Pavellons Guell with Gaudi's dragon gate, all in one walk, 1.2 km west of bcn_007. A future pass should take this as a single unit rather than tree by tree, and must check the

trees.name: The Vil-la Amelia and Sarria cluster
trees.species: Schinus molle; Phoenix canariensis; Platanus x acerifolia; Eucalyptus globulus
trees.note: Four register entries inside one public Sarria garden, 900 m from the Pedralbes cluster above. Not evaluated this pass. The eucalyptus and the plane are single-unit; the palms are a group and would need the collectible-point test.

trees.name: Lledoner de la Fundacio Munoz Ramonet
trees.note: Access unverified. The Munoz Ramonet gardens passed to the city and open to the public on a limited schedule; that needs confirming before this counts as publicly accessible. Undated in the candidate list.

trees.name: Figuera de la Facultat de Dret
trees.note: On the university law faculty grounds. The campus is open in practice but the register does not say so, and the entry is undated. Sits inside the Pedralbes cluster above, so resolve it with that pass.

trees.name: Huingan del carrer Joaquim Blume
trees.note: Species dispute, and it is the only thing holding this back. The city register says Schinus longifolia, an Argentine species; OSM node 4506714524, surveyed from the same catalogue, says Schinus polygamus; and huingan, the common name the city itself uses, is the Chilean name for S. polygama. With the build now failing on species naming, shipping a tree under a contested binomial is not worth it. E

trees.name: Araucaria de l'avinguda Francesc Ferrer i Guardia
trees.note: 1920 and 24 m tall, which would make it a good sixth stop on the Montjuic walk, but it has no second source of any kind. It is a recent catalogue entry with no bcnsostenible page, no guia.barcelona page, no OSM node within 400 m and an empty ownership field, so neither the age, the position nor the public access can be corroborated. Everything rests on one line in the open data file.

trees.name: Grevillea dels jardins dels Drets Humans
trees.note: The largest untouched single tree left in the register: girth 4.1 m and 32 m tall, on public ground. Undated, which is the only reason it is here, and it sits 1.4 km south of the botanical garden in La Marina de Port, off the Montjuic walk. A silky oak that size would carry a page on its own if a date or a second source turns up.

trees.name: Eritrina dels jardins Mossen Costa i Llobera
trees.note: Girth 3 m and a 20 m crown, public, in the free cactus garden on the sea side of Montjuic, which is a real destination in its own right. Undated in the register and no second source found this pass. The obvious anchor for a second Montjuic walk on the Miramar side, together with the Iuca filifera below.

trees.name: Iuca filifera dels jardins de Mossen Costa i Llobera
trees.note: Undated, and a yucca is a marginal call as a collectible tree. Kept because it stands beside the Erythrina caffra above in the same free garden and the pair would make that side of the hill worth a walk.

trees.name: Carpi del jardi Botanic Historic
trees.note: 1924, 20 m tall, in the same ravine as bcn_005, bcn_006, bcn_021 and bcn_022. Ownership reads Privat, which here means the museum owns the land rather than that the gate is shut, the same as bcn_006. Held purely on count: five entries in one quarry pit behind one paid gate is too many.

trees.name: Alvocater del Teatre Lliure
trees.note: 1946, so 80 years, under the bar. An avocado tree outside a theatre on the Montjuic walk is a good story waiting for the age rule to soften. OSM node 4203274163 confirms the position.

trees.name: Acacia del Japo del carrer Guardia Urbana
trees.note: On the Montjuic walk between the Teatre Grec and Placa Carles Buigas, girth 2.3 m and 20 m tall, but the register's age field reads 'En estudi', under study. No date, no page.

trees.name: Melaleuca dels jardins de Petra Kelly
trees.note: Undated, 4 m tall and a 1.88 m girth, which is a broad low shrub rather than a tree. Recorded for completeness.

trees.name: Lledoner dels jardins dels Drets Humans
trees.note: Girth 2.9 m, public, undated. Sits 130 m from the Grevillea above, so the two would open a small walk in La Marina de Port if either gets a date.

trees.name: Tarongers de Louisiana dels jardins de la Torre Girona
trees.note: Incidental find while verifying the Torre Girona cluster (2026-08-06 Barcelona deepen pass): a 14-unit register entry in the same garden as bcn_026/027/028, but the register gives no planting year and no ownership field, and no independent source was checked this pass. Kept here as the folded id per the Setubal-twins precedent, in case a future pass ever wants to split them.

Blocked, not a lead: this would be a c.30-year-old sapling, nothing close to the ancient/remarkable bar, not registered, and not separately located in any source found this pass.

trees.name: The second Turner's Oak of Parc d'Egmont
trees.note: Third thickest of its species in the region, 23 metres tall against its neighbour's 10, and on the same lawns as bru_011. Held back only because two Turner's oaks four hundred metres apart would read as one entry told twice. If Parc d'Egmont ever justifies a page of its own, this is the first addition.

trees.name: London Plane of Parc d'Egmont [RESOLVED 2026-08-14, delivered as bru_017]
trees.note: Second thickest tree in the park after the sycamore, but ranked only 98th of its species in the region, and the register's per-tree page carries no height. A good tree with nothing yet to say about it.

trees.name: Horse Chestnut of Parc d'Egmont [RESOLVED 2026-08-14, delivered as bru_018]
trees.note: 90th of its species in the region and the only tree in the cluster whose heritage page failed to render its site block on fetch, so the site attribution is from the dataset alone. bru_010 already covers horse chestnut for Brussels.

trees.name: Oriental Plane of Parc d'Egmont [RESOLVED 2026-08-14, delivered as bru_019]
trees.note: Named on the park's own information panel, 22 metres tall, 21st of its species in the region. Skipped only because bru_003, the Parc Leopold oriental plane, is the thickest of its species in the entire region and would make this one look like a repeat.

trees.name: The beeches of Parc d'Egmont
trees.note: Brussels Environment's published Egmont walk stops at one beech with an enormous flared root plate and gives it register id 632, which does not exist in the 2026 open dataset at all. The four beeches that do exist in the park sit within 60 metres of the walk's coordinate and cannot be told apart from the description. Resolvable in one visit or one call to the region; not publishable until the id i

trees.name: The White Mulberries of the Passage de Milan gate
trees.note: Eighth thickest white mulberry in the region and a genuine story, that Belgium tried and failed to build a silk industry on this species about a century ago, but they stand as a pair flanking a gate rather than as one tree, and bru_009 already gives Brussels a mulberry. Fruit in July if the birds leave any.

trees.name: The pyramidal holly of Parc d'Egmont
trees.note: Second largest of its cultivar in the region and signposted on the park's own panel. A holly at 140cm girth is unusual, but it is a shrub-scale tree that will not read as a destination beside a 32 metre sycamore in the same park.

trees.name: Kentucky Coffeetree of Parc d'Egmont [RESOLVED 2026-08-14, delivered as bru_020]
trees.note: Fourth largest of its species in the region on a girth of only 73cm, which says how rare the species is here rather than how big this tree is. Too young to stand in front of; worth revisiting in a decade.

trees.name: The 2019 additions to the Egmont inventory
trees.species: Sophora japonica, Fraxinus excelsior f. pendula, Gleditsia triacanthos var. inermis
trees.note: Three trees surveyed in July 2019, all under 165cm, all ranked in the top thirty of their species in the region because those species are uncommon in Brussels. Real trees, thin stories, and the register gives no height for any of the three.

trees.name: The Tree of Heaven of the Grand Sablon
trees.note: The best single lead left in this quarter and the one most worth someone's time. Ninth thickest of its species in the region, 19 metres tall with a nine metre clean trunk, standing on Brussels' antiques square, and legally protected: the most notorious invasive tree in Europe listed as a monument on the city's most expensive place. Measured in 2025, so it was certainly alive then. Held back for on

trees.name: The Turkish Hazel of the Grand Sablon
trees.note: Eleventh of its species in the region, 17 metres tall with a 16 metre crown, recorded as fully healthy, and the register describes it as an isolated tree holding a central position in the landscape, which is exactly the collectible-point test passing. Same single-source problem as the ailanthus above. Note the register's coordinate for this one was not re-derived in this pass; take it from the dat

trees.name: Horse Chestnut and Caucasian Lime of the Grand Sablon
trees.note: Both on the square, both middling in their species rankings, both single-sourced. They would thicken a Sablon walk rather than justify one.

trees.name: The Silver Maple and Pagoda Tree of Place Jean Jacobs
trees.note: A tiny square between the Sablon and the Palace of Justice, two registered trees, both described as holding a central position in the landscape. The silver maple's health is recorded as 'Defauts moyens', middling defects, which is the worst rating anywhere in this cluster and needs checking before it could ship. bru_008 already gives Brussels a pagoda tree.

trees.name: Where to deepen Brussels next
trees.note: The register's four walkable clusters hold 577 of its 582 trees, and this pass worked one corner of one of them. The three richest untouched sub-clusters, by count of registered trees within 400 metres: Parc Leopold and its slope, 41 trees, where bru_003 already stands alone and where a second and third entry would turn one pin into a walk. The Laeken and Osseghem parks in the north, 34 trees incl

trees.name: Cedro-do-Bucaco at the Passo da 1a Queda
trees.note: [RESOLVED 2026-08-13, delivered as bsc_007] The best unshipped tree here and the first one a next pass should chase. Register gives 300 years at the 2016 measurement, so about 310 now, with a 5.26 m trunk and 31 m of height, which would make it the second oldest thing in the forest after the Cedro de Sao Jose and, unlike that one, structurally intact. Cut only because no independent source names t

trees.name: Pedunculate Oak by the Capela de Sao Pedro
trees.note: [RESOLVED 2026-08-13, delivered as bsc_008] Register gives 300 years at the 2016 measurement, so about 310 now, girth 4.92 m, height 24 m, crown 20.7 m. One of only two natives on the classified list and it would balance a page otherwise made entirely of imports. No independent source found for the individual tree in the time available.

trees.name: Redwood at the Fonte de Santa Teresa
trees.note: Girth 5.58 m, 45 m tall, 150 years at the 2016 measurement. Bigger in the trunk than the pair published as bsc_005 and on the Trilho da Agua past the historic fountains, so a genuinely good stop. Cut on the count and because a page with three separate redwood entries stops being a walk and becomes a list.

trees.name: Redwood near the Porta das Lapas
trees.note: Girth 5.04 m, 45 m tall, no age recorded. Register places it 70 m from the Porta das Lapas on the path to the Lago Grande, which is the far west of the walled forest, about 450 m off the published walk. Cut on distance and count.

trees.name: Redwood on the bend at the head of the Vale de Sao Silvestre
trees.note: Girth 4.67 m and 56 m tall, the tallest redwood in the register here, 147 years at 2016. Registered as tipo Alameda, so it may be one of a row rather than a single tree, which has to be resolved on the ground before it could ship as a collectible point. Ten metres from King Regnans, so it may in practice be part of that stop.

trees.name: American Ash at the Largo do Mosteiro
trees.note: Girth 4.65 m, 24 m tall, crown 26 m wide, 136 years at 2016. Stands right by the Loja da Mata, so it is on the walk anyway and costs nothing to add. Cut for lack of a second source and because the Largo do Mosteiro already contributes two published entries.

trees.name: Sycamore Maple by the Lago da Fonte
trees.note: The best best_time candidate in Bucaco and the only obvious one: 36 m of deciduous tree at 100 years in 2016, so genuine autumn colour in a forest whose published trees are all evergreen. Cut for lack of a second source. Worth chasing precisely because this page carries no seasonal peak at all.

trees.name: Cork Oak on the south slope of the Lago Grande
trees.note: [RESOLVED 2026-08-13, delivered as bsc_009] Girth 4.26 m, 17.5 m tall, no age in the register. A native cork oak inside a collection of exotics, and cork oak is the Portuguese tree, so the story writes itself. No second source and no age; 400 m west of the published walk.

trees.name: Til by the Lago Grande
trees.note: Ocotea foetens, the til of the Madeiran and Canarian laurel forests, 38 m tall with a 3 m trunk. A relict laurisilva species growing on the mainland is a genuinely unusual thing to stand in front of. No age recorded, no second source.

trees.name: Cedro-do-Bucaco by the Passo de Anas
trees.note: Girth 3.68 m, 27 m tall, crown 19 m, no age recorded. Undated and smaller than the other cypresses; on the Via Sacra path so easy to fold into a future walk.

trees.name: Cedro-do-Bucaco by the ruin of the Ermida do Sacramento
trees.note: Girth 4.2 m, 27 m tall, crown 20.2 m, no age. Standing beside a ruined hermitage 30 m from the Passo de Anas, which is a good setting. Undated and single-sourced.

trees.name: Cedro-do-Bucaco east of the Casa de Guarda do Serpa
trees.note: Girth 4.72 m, 35 m tall, 100 years. Not part of the 2018 classification decree (no classified date in the register), so its protected status differs from the rest and needs checking. About 200 m east of a forest guard house on a forest track, at the north edge of the cluster.

trees.name: Mexican White Pine at the Cova da Raposa
trees.note: Pinus ayacahuite, girth 2.55 m, 40 m tall, 100 years. Not in the 2018 decree. Modest trunk; ships only if a story turns up.

trees.name: Mexican White Pine behind the Passo de Anas
trees.note: REGISTER DATA ERROR, do not repeat the figure. The register gives height 100 m against a girth of 1.95 m, which is physically impossible and would beat every tree in Europe. Almost certainly a decimal or unit slip for 10.0 m. Recorded here so a future pass does not rediscover it as a sensation.

trees.name: Magenta Cherry at the nursery entrance
trees.note: Syzygium paniculatum, girth 3.15 m, crown 9.4 m, no height and no age recorded. An Australian rainforest tree with edible magenta fruit, which would be a real fruit best_time if a source dated the season here. Too thin as it stands.

No sour

trees.species: Cedar (Cedrus sp., species not specified by the register)

trees.name: Red River Gum of the Celia Mendez Garden
trees.note: The thickest trunk in the whole municipal catalogue at 4.86m girth and 34.8m tall, a relict of the riverside market gardens. Undated, no photo, peripheral neighbourhood 3km east, and no story beyond size. Strong candidate the day Cordoba grows past seven.

trees.name: Ash of Santa Marina
trees.note: Two sources and real history (documented in Los Arboles de Cordoba, 1984, and the 2002 provincial inventory; local botanist Rafa Tamajon argues it is centenarian). But only 9.5m tall with visible trunk decay and declining. Latitude was lost in the catalogue PDF extraction and needs recovering from the page image.

trees.name: Chinaberry at the Puerta de Almodovar
trees.note: 24.5m tall casting 400 square metres of shade, about 72 years old now. Handsome, young, no story yet.

trees.name: Cypress at the Alcazar entrance
trees.note: 26.5m tall on a crown only 3.5m wide, a green needle, and free to see outside the ticket gate. About 77 years old, so young for us, but visually the most striking of Cordoba's modern trees.

trees.name: Stone Pine of Santa Maria de Trassierra
trees.note: 3.26m girth, 25m, roughly 90 years. Reachable by Aucorsa line L-T in about 19 minutes but only about five services a day, which strains the day-trip boundary.

trees.name: Photinia at the Palacio de la Merced
trees.note: A naturalists' walk claims it is the oldest specimen of its species in the province. Not in the municipal catalogue and unverified. One follow-up search would settle it.

trees.name: Casuarinas of the Plaza de Jeronimo Paez
trees.note: Three trees, the tallest above 30m, five minutes from the Mezquita. Single-sourced to the municipal catalogue with no independent second source and no published age.

trees.name: Himalayan Cedar of the Plaza del Cardenal Toledo
trees.note: 22.5m and the near-sole occupant of its square, about 102 years old, and it predates the 1945 garden around it. Single-sourced, no photo.

trees.name: Siberian Elm of the Alcazar
trees.note: 27m against a species maximum of 15m, genuinely exceptional. Single-sourced and behind a paid gate, though the gardens are free on summer mornings.

trees.name: Canary Palm of the Doctor Emilio Luque Square
trees.note: Around 112 years and among the oldest palms in the city. Single-sourced, and the catalogue names red palm weevil as the threat that has killed dozens of Cordoba's Canary palms, so survival needs checking before anything is published.

trees.name: Ginkgo of the Agriculture Gardens
trees.note: About 72 years, the oldest ginkgo in Cordoba's public gardens and a landmark for the city's botany students. Young, and no photo.

trees.name: Olive of the Agriculture Gardens
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Looks perfect on paper at 2.6m girth, and it is the tree the naturalists' walk stops at, but the municipal catalogue itself says it has barely any history: it was installed on 30 April 2009, transplanted from Castellon. An old tree in the wrong city. This is the trap in Cordoba olive research; do not confuse it with the Patio de los Naranjos olive.

trees.name: The private patios of the Patios Festival
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as ordinary entries. UNESCO-listed and full of old citrus, but open only during the May festival. Hard rule 10 restricted access; if ever used, the restriction must be stated in the entry itself.

trees.name: Sotos de la Albolafia
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A protected Natural Monument of 21 hectares of riverside woodland between the Roman and San Rafael bridges. No single identifiable tree and no trunk to stand at, so it fails the collectible-point test exactly as a long avenue does.

trees.name: Hackberries of Santa Maria de Trassierra
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Base girths to 5.97m, but condition rated bad to very bad, systematically pollarded, and built into the boundary walls of private houses. Private-land risk with no viewing point.

trees.name: Molle and swamp cypress of Cordoba Zoo
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Inside a paid zoo, and the molle stands inside a gibbon enclosure.

trees.name: Pecan of El Arenal
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. On a fenced empty lot.

trees.name: Tetraclinis of the Patio de los Naranjos
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Recorded as disappeared.

Giant Redwood, edge of Physics Lawn

The Stone Pine of the Bobolino
trees.note: MASAF 14/D612/FI/09, girth 412 cm, height 31.5 m. Stands about 25 m from the live flo_007 and 45 m from flo_015, so it is the single cheapest addition left in Florence: a visitor already standing at the Bobolino cedars would not take a step. Held back only for want of a genuinely independent second source. The comune's list and the intoscana article that reports it both derive from the same MASAF

trees.name: The Monterey Cypress of the Giardino Simone Weil
trees.note: MASAF 15/D612/FI/09, girth 388 cm, height 18.5 m, in a free public garden about 90 m from the Bobolino cluster. Same problem as the stone pine above: one register, no independent corroboration found in this pass. Monterey cypress is a striking species with a tiny native range on the California coast, so it would earn its place on the story alone if a second source turns up.

trees.name: The Cypress of the Monte alle Croci Steps
trees.note: MASAF 19/D612/FI/09, girth 346 cm, height 21.5 m. Sits on the stepped pilgrim climb from Piazza Poggi up to San Miniato al Monte, about 250 m from the live flo_009 ginkgo at Piazzale Michelangelo, so it would join the two hillside stops into a continuous route. Only the register and its municipal republication were found, which is one source. Worth one targeted search on the Via del Monte alle Cro

trees.name: The Aleppo Pine of Via Giramondino
trees.note: MASAF 17/D612/FI/09, girth 323 cm, height 22.5 m, on Viale Galileo roughly midway between the Bobolino cluster and Piazzale Michelangelo. Would be the connecting stop on Poggi's Viale dei Colli walk. Single-sourced, and the smallest girth of the hillside candidates, so it is the weakest of the four on merit as well as on evidence.

trees.name: The Strawberry Tree of the Giardino dell'Iris
trees.note: MASAF 18/D612/FI/09, height 8.0 m, and the register records no girth at all. Stands about 40 m from the live flo_009 ginkgo, which is as tight as a pairing gets. Two problems, neither fatal: no girth and no age in any source found, and the Giardino dell'Iris opens only for a few weeks around the iris flowering each spring, so the access field would have to say so plainly and the season would effec

trees.name: The Chilean Wine Palm of Villa di Rusciano
trees.note: MASAF 22/D612/FI/09, girth 349 cm, height 15.5 m. A genuinely uncommon species in Europe and a good story (the sap was tapped for palm honey until the species was nearly wiped out in Chile), in a municipal villa park. Failed on the count and on distance rather than on quality: it is about 1.6 km east of the Piazzale Michelangelo stop, so it does not join either existing walk. Keep for a third Flor

trees.name: The Three Hackberries of the Cascine
trees.note: MASAF 54, 55 and 56/D612/FI/09, girths 407, 397 and 355 cm, standing within 25 m of one another at Piazza Vasari. REGISTER TRAP, recorded so the next pass does not repeat the work: these are three separate register entries for what a visitor sees as one group, exactly the double-counting pattern Setubal produced. If they ship they ship as ONE entry describing the group, with the other two sheet id

trees.name: The Cypress of Villa della Petraia
trees.note: MASAF 10/D612/FI/09, girth 580 cm, the second largest girth in the whole comune after the Montezuma cypress. Villa della Petraia is a Medici villa, a UNESCO site and open to the public, so access is fine. Failed purely on distance: 5 km north of the centre, joins no walk, and would repeat the scattering problem the live page already has. A strong candidate for a Medici villas collection rather tha

trees.name: The Black Pine of Villa Gamberaia

They would extend the tightest cluster on the site at zero walking cost. Not pursued this pass because the pass was scoped to the MASAF candidates and the count was already met, and because each needs its own second source. Note the site already has phenology files f

trees.name: Sakamoto no Mukunoki
trees.note: Dazaifu city designation 2015, 25.5m tall, 3.65m girth, roots exposed and spreading seven metres, and it has a full street address (Sakamoto 3-268-1), which makes it the most precisely placeable untouched tree in the region. One more pass would ship it.

trees.name: The Great Yamamomo of Kanetake
trees.note: Prefectural designation, 4.7m girth, individually mapped. Nishi ward, needs a second source and a photo.

trees.name: The Camphor of Shimizu
trees.note: 9.7m girth in Minami ward, which would be among the city's largest. No coordinate, no second source yet.

trees.name: The Married Camphors and Great Ginkgo of Torikai Hachimangu
trees.note: Two individually mapped trees at one shrine, so pins exist, but no age, no measurements and no open-licence photograph of either.

trees.name: Hibaru Sakura
trees.note: Thirteen cherries, so it fails the collectible-point test as a city entry, but the story is one of the best in Fukuoka: in 1984 someone tied a tanka to a trunk to protest the felling, the mayor replied in verse and the plan was dropped. Belongs in a collection rather than on the city page. Also unresolved whether all eight originals still live.

trees.name: The Camphor of Hakozaki-gu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP without a current on-site check. The city's largest at 11.4m girth and 800 years claimed, but a March 2025 surveyor wrote that he could not tell whether it is still alive: trunk and branches so smothered by a climbing fig that no camphor foliage is visible, severe hollowing, front roots dead, vigour rated two out of five.

trees.name: Hakomatsu of Hakozaki-gu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. The present pine is a replacement of unknown generation. Context inside another story at most.

trees.name: Kankakeshii of Kashii-gu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Kaibara Ekiken already recorded in the Edo period that the tree standing then had been grown from the old one's seed. Alive and visitable, but only ever a footnote.

trees.name: Tenjin no Mori, Dazaifu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as one entry. A prefectural designation covering 51 camphors across the grounds. Story material for the great camphor, not an entry.

trees.name: Tachibanayama camphor primeval forest
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as one entry. A special natural monument of roughly 3,000 camphors. Only the named Tachibanayama Great Camphor inside it could qualify, and that needs a bus plus a 40 minute climb.

trees.name: The Chokushi-michi camphor avenue, Kashii
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Saplings donated and planted in 1926, so about a century old, and an avenue.

trees.name: The Hobashira-seki of Najima
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A fossilised trunk.

trees.name: The Chishanoki of Komyozen-ji
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as visitable. The temple has been closed to the public since 2018 for precinct works with no confirmed reopening.

trees.name: The Mukunoki of Kouun Shrine, Nishi Park
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as told. Presented locally as the tree that survived the 1945 air raid, but no age, no measurements and only tourism blogs, and part of it was cut back around 2021 as a breakage risk. Note for the whole city: there is no Fukuoka equivalent of the Hiroshima survivor-tree registry, so no Fukuoka tree may be given an air-raid survival story.

trees.name: The Choja no Fuji of Musashi-ji
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A wisteria vine, and about 45 minutes out.

trees.name: Chilean Wine Palm of Villa Durazzo Pallavicini
trees.note: Register only (MASAF sheet 11/D969/GE/07, girth 385cm, height 14m). The Ministry of Culture's own page on the park names the camphor and the cedar specifically but not this palm, so no independent corroboration turned up this pass. Same park as the two delivered trees (gnv_009, gnv_010); worth a second look before the city page ships, since a third tree here would strengthen an already-good pocket

trees.name: Second Cinnamomum glanduliferum of Villa Durazzo Pallavicini
trees.note: Register only (MASAF sheet 12/D969/GE/07, girth 392cm, height 20m), same coordinates as the palm above. Same park already has one Cinnamomum-family tree delivered (the camphor, gnv_009) and one already-flagged Cinnamomum glanduliferum at Via Romolo Gessi (gnv_004); a third of similar species this close together risks reading as padding rather than a distinct entry unless it's visibly a different,

trees.name: Bidwill's Pine (Queensland Pine) at Villa Groppallo, Nervi

Nervi is roughly 10km east of the centre and does

trees.name: Cedar of Lebanon, Piazza Chiesa Acquasanta
trees.note: Register only (MASAF sheet 16/D969/GE/07, girth 461cm, height 25m), 13.2km from the centre point in the Val Varenna hills, and does not join any other candidate. Larger girth than either Villa Pallavicini cedar, so worth a look if Acquasanta ever gets its own research pass, but not part of a walkable cluster this pass could support.

trees.name: The Old Trees of Santa Marinha da Costa
trees.species: Pedunculate Oak (Quercus robur), with Atlas Cedar, Northern Red Oak, Sweet Chestnut, Mexican Cypress and Blue Gum as companions in the same classified conjunto
trees.note: The research pass's own recommendation was to ship this, and it is genuinely a strong tree: an oak beside a baroque water tank in the walled garden of a 12th-century monastery, classified public-interest since 1940. Held back on publication (not by the research pass, on review) because the site is now a hotel (Pousada de Santa Marinha) and no source found states plainly that a non-guest can walk i

trees.name: The Camellias of Casa de Margaride
trees.species: Camellia japonica L.; Camellia reticulata Lindl. (plus Ilex aquifolium, Taxus baccata, Chamaecyparis lawsoniana, Cupressus lusitanica in the same garden-conjunto entry)
trees.note: Genuinely remarkable: rare 18th/19th-century European camellia cultivars (Alba Plena, Variegata, Pompone, Elegans, Lavinia Maggi, the Portuguese 1889 cultivar 'Augusto Leal Gouveia Pinto'), one specimen won Portuguese Tree of the Year 2024, house and garden classified Monument of Public Interest 2012, trees classified 2022 (Despacho 837/2022). Four register rows here (cameleira, the garden-conjunt

trees.name: The Camellia of Casa da Covilha
trees.note: Register's single oldest dated tree in the whole Guimaraes set: 300 years at last measurement (2018), girth 3.6m. House and quinta (17th century, remodelled by architect Fernando Tavora in the 1970s) classified Monument of Public Interest. Same access problem as Margaride: private house in Fermentoes, guided visits organized by the family (with José Bernardo Tavora), no standing public hours found

trees.name: The Arboretum of Casa da Ribeira
trees.species: Pinus strobus; Sequoia sempervirens; Cupressus lusitanica; Cedrus deodara; Quercus robur; Fagus sylvatica; Liriodendron tulipifera; Liquidambar styraciflua
trees.note: 8-species conjunto arboreo, classified 2020 (Despacho 6069/2020). 5.3km from the historic centre, well outside any cluster with the shipped trees and unresearched this pass. A candidate for its own future pass rather than a Guimaraes-centre addition.

trees.name: Stone Pine of Rua 25 de Abril, Silvares
trees.note: Single tree on a roundabout, ~4.4km from the centre, age 100 at 2011 measurement. Unresearched, out of cluster range.

trees.name: Stone Pine of Moreira de Conegos

trees.name: The bald cypress twins and the Balearic box of the Orto Botanico

trees.name: Great Zelkova of Kasuga
trees.note: 4.9m girth, the largest zelkova in Nara Park, hollow and mossy. Single-sourced to the shrine's own forest-walk page, no coordinate, no age, and 'upper portions lost' needs checking that it is thriving rather than a relic.

trees.name: Cycad of Jokyo-ji
trees.note: Nara City Natural Monument, 1979, and close to the station. Small tree at a minor temple, thin sourcing, visitor access unverified.

trees.name: Bayberry of Oryu-ji
trees.note: Nara City Natural Monument, 1979. Same profile as the cycad: real designation, thin sourcing, access unverified.

trees.name: Persimmon of Jigen-ji
trees.note: Nara City Natural Monument, 1983. Real designation, thin sourcing, access unverified.

trees.name: Ichiigashi of the Kasugayama primeval forest
trees.note: 6.00m girth and 35m on the southern path, which would be a strong entry, but one source and no coordinate. A single named tree inside the forest can qualify even though the forest cannot.

trees.name: Yogo-no-Matsu, Kasuga Taisha
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. The original pine died in 1995; a successor sapling grows beside the surviving stump. Famous as the claimed origin of the pine painted on every Noh stage, though even that attribution is disputed as a later invention.

trees.name: Chisokuin Nara-no-Yaezakura
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. The tree designated a national Natural Monument in 1923 has died; today's cherries are propagated descendants. Chisokuin is a closed sub-temple open roughly one day a year.

trees.name: Kasugayama Primeval Forest
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as one entry. A Special Natural Monument covering a whole mountain, with no single tree and nowhere to stand. A named individual inside it can qualify separately.

trees.name: Kasuga Ichiigashi giant-tree group
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Thirty-plus separate trees over 3m girth scattered across the precinct, designated as a group. No single destination.

trees.name: Sunazuri-no-Fuji
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A wisteria vine on a trellis.

trees.name: Shoryaku-ji Kojii grove
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A prefecturally designated grove rather than one tree, and Bodaisen-cho is well beyond the day-trip boundary.

trees.name: Takiyama left-spiral Torreya
trees.note: NEVER SHIP for Nara. A prefectural Natural Monument, but in Tsuge-Hayama-cho, inside the municipal boundary only through a merger and far over 30 minutes out.

trees.name: Tsukigase Oyama ancient plums
trees.reason: out of range, and an ensemble
trees.note: NEVER SHIP for Nara. City-designated in March 2026, but Tsukigase is roughly an hour out, and it is a group rather than one tree.

trees.name: The thousand-year cedar at the Kasuga Treasure Hall cafe
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A cut stump on indoor display. Easy to confuse with the living great cedar, which is why it is recorded here.

Skipped in favour of the older, better-documented n.1 (pad_003) to avoid two near-identical ginkgo entries on one page; worth considering only if the city needs to grow past its current cluster count.

trees.name: Cedro di via Michelangelo
trees.note: RAMI gives it ~105 years and only local-level designation, and the species is recorded merely as 'Cedrus sp.' Too young and too thinly identified to clear the bar while better candidates sit in the two central clusters. Keep for a later pass that grows the city.

trees.note: Six MASAF trees sitting together about 10 km east of Padova, almost certainly in a Brenta villa park. Inside the 30-minute day-trip boundary and dense enough to be its own walk, but it is a different place with a different name and belongs to a separate pass rather than padded onto a Padova page.

trees.name: Jilm vaz v Michelskem lese

trees.name: Duby letni na Pavim vrchu
trees.note: Three memorial oaks of 270 to 410 cm on Na Plani in Smichov, the surviving remnant of the hill's original woodland, 1.5 km south of the route. Recorded as a group of three rather than one identifiable tree, so as it stands it fails the collectible-point test. If a future pass can establish which of the three is the largest and give it its own position, that one alone would qualify.

trees.name: Platan javorolisty v parku Jezerka
trees.note: Pamatny strom, 525 cm, below the Divadlo na Jezerce in Nusle, predating the park built around it from 1949. Big enough to matter and in a public park, but it is a fifth plane in a city whose page is already plane-heavy and it sits alone 3 km southeast of everything else. A candidate for a Nusle and Vinohrady cluster, not for the centre.

trees.name: Jilm Na Zatorach v Holesovicich
trees.note: Vyznamny strom 28, 266 cm, by the bus turning circle at Nadrazi Holesovice, the last trace of the Zatory quarter that was demolished in 1978. A good story about a place rather than about a tree, and 4 km from the centre, but it would join the Stromovka and Cisarsky ostrov pair (prg_006 and prg_007) into a three-stop northern walk.

trees.name: Moruse v ulici Nad Hradnim vodojemem
trees.note: Vyznamny strom 19, 255 cm, in Stresovice, recorded as the largest white mulberry in Prague. A species we do not have anywhere in the city and a genuine July fruit peak, which the season radar is short of. Failed on position: it stands in a residential street 3 km west of the centre with nothing else near it, and on evidence, since no second source was looked for this pass.

trees.name: The Cedar of Lebanon of Marques de la Cadena
trees.note: Privately owned, at the corner of Calle San Juan de la Pena and Marques de la Cadena in Arrabal. Named in the book's dedication as one of the trees saved by local pressure, which makes it a good story on someone else's land.
